author: Greg McVerry
body_html:
When I started working on @Mozilla leadership curriculum on MoFo side I kept pointing out MoCo doing same thing. It was leadershsip and how to work open kind of stuff.

Tried to be a bridge to both but contributing to MoCo became easier for me because all the sites were written in HTML and styled with CSS.

As someone just learning, having a model MADE huge difference. Literally helped me learn the web.

Every single thing I know today started because of Mozilla's commitment to an HTML first web.

I couldn't remix curriculum for MoFo anymore. React added in layers of complexity that made my efforts impossible.

Much of this could have been avoided by simply using HTML and CSS. We are talking lesson plans....a couple paragraphs, and bulleted lists (much like web documentation). ....There was no need for complicated frameworks that drove contributors away.

You don't strap rocket engines to your shows when walking in the woods. You match tool to task and enjoy the simplicity your labor provides.

Time and Treasure got wasted and nobody looked up to see the forest.

Then on the MoCo side I got to see the same(ish) curriculum. Each lesson it's own page. Documentation was written in HTML and styled with CSS.

More importantly, as a team on the MoCo side (was Participation Team at time) we could ship faster and more reliable products. On MoFo React curriculum we would be waiting for a new developer to up their skills, deal with constant framework versioning, waiting for a DevOp or SecOp, and be done for when the one person on the team who knew the framework du jour left.

It affirmed my commitment to Mozilla after what had been really turbulent times on the MoFo learning team. I saw a people driven to support a sustainable web for the long haul.

I hear people talking about the web changing and "modern new front-end developer frameworks." How are a vision of the archaic web is over and folks have moved on.

I don't want the web we have now.

I hope somebody will be at Mozilla, like the Participation Team did for me, to point wayward travelers back to a human-readable web.

Write documentation in HTML. Make documentation pretty with CSS.
